UnitStatement: SPEC is the authoritative specification for physical structures, file formats, schemas, and layout conventions in the Chirality filesystem-as-state project execution system.
All Chirality agents, tools, and governance documents reference SPEC.
When an agent instruction file defines a format inline, SPEC is the canonical version and agent instructions must conform.
Normative keywords in SPEC follow the conventions defined in AGENT_HELPS_HUMANS.md.
SPEC embodies the four-pillar philosophy defined in DIRECTIVE.md section 2.
SPEC sections instantiate the DIRECTIVE pillars.
The Ontology pillar maps to SPEC sections 1-2 and 10, governing execution root layout, deliverable structure, and filesystem-safe naming.
The Epistemology pillar maps to SPEC sections 5-6 and 14-15, governing dependency tracking, provenance requirements, evidence schema, and conflict resolution mechanisms.
The Praxiology pillar maps to SPEC sections 3-4, 9, and 11-12, governing lifecycle state, context and authority, agent instruction structure, and validation.
The Axiology pillar maps to SPEC sections 7-8 and 13, governing reference management, memory management, coordination representation, and schema values.
SPEC alignment ensures project execution state reflects the same philosophical commitments as the governance framework.
An execution instance is a self-contained project workspace rooted at {EXECUTION_ROOT}/.
The execution root contains packages and tool roots for derived or operational outputs.
INIT.md stores session initialization parameters at the execution root.
PKG-XX_{PkgLabel}/ represents one or more packages under the execution root.
0_References/ stores package-level reference materials.
1_Working/ stores active deliverable folders.
2_Checking/ is the review staging area and contains From/ and To/ subfolders.
3_Issued/ stores released deliverables.
_Aggregation/ stores aggregation snapshots.
_Change/ stores change management records.
_Coordination/ stores coordination representation, including _COORDINATION.md.
_Decomposition/ stores project decomposition documents.
_Archive/ stores baseline snapshots with checksums.
_Sources/ stores shared source and reference documents.
Package folder names use the {PKG-ID}_{PkgLabel}/ pattern.
PKG-ID follows the PKG-XX format.
PkgLabel is a filesystem-safe version of the package name.
The 0_References/ package subfolder is required for package-level reference materials.
The 0_References/_Archive/ package subfolder is required for archived references.
The 1_Working/ package subfolder is required for active deliverable folders.
The 1_Working/_Archive/ package subfolder is required for archived working drafts.
The 2_Checking/ package subfolder is required as a review staging area.
The 2_Checking/From/ package subfolder is required for incoming review items.
The 2_Checking/To/ package subfolder is required for outgoing review items.
The 3_Issued/ package subfolder is required for released deliverables.
The 3_Issued/_Archive/ package subfolder is required for archived issued versions.
Tool roots are project-level directories for derived outputs.
Each tool root is isolated from source truth in deliverable folders.
_Aggregation/ is the tool root for aggregation snapshots and templates and is typically written by AGGREGATION.
_Change/ is the tool root for change management records and is typically written by CHANGE.
_Coordination/ is the tool root for coordination representation and is typically written by ORCHESTRATOR.
_Decomposition/ is the tool root for project decomposition documents and is typically written by PROJECT_DECOMP.
_Estimates/ is the tool root for cost estimate snapshots and is typically written by ESTIMATING.
_Reconciliation/ is the tool root for reconciliation reports and closure analysis and is typically written by RECONCILIATION.
_Archive/ is the tool root for baseline snapshots with checksums and is typically written by a human or CHANGE.
_Scripts/ is the tool root for deployment and analysis scripts and is typically written by humans or tooling.
_Sources/ is the tool root for shared source and reference documents and is typically written by humans.
Each deliverable occupies {EXECUTION_ROOT}/{PKG-ID}_{PkgLabel}/1_Working/{DEL-ID}_{DelLabel}/.
_STATUS.md must be present in each deliverable and is created by PREPARATION for lifecycle state and history.
_CONTEXT.md must be present in each deliverable and is created by PREPARATION for identity, decomposition pointer, and traceability.
_DEPENDENCIES.md must be present in each deliverable and is created by PREPARATION for dependency summary.
_REFERENCES.md must be present in each deliverable and is created by PREPARATION for source document pointers.
Datasheet.md must be present in each deliverable and is created by TASK+four-documents for key parameters and structured metadata.
Specification.md must be present in each deliverable and is created by TASK+four-documents for technical requirements and scope definition.
Guidance.md must be present in each deliverable and is created by TASK+four-documents for design guidance, rationale, and best practices.
Procedure.md must be present in each deliverable and is created by TASK+four-documents for step-by-step execution workflow.
Dependencies.csv should be present when TASK+dependency-extract produces a structured dependency register using the v3.1 schema.
_MEMORY.md should be present when PREPARATION creates shared working memory for WORKING_ITEMS and deliverable-local task agents.
_SEMANTIC.md may be present when TASK+semantic-matrix-build produces a semantic lens with derivation work.
_SEMANTIC_LENSING.md may be present when TASK+lens-register produces semantic analysis narrative.
MEMORY.md may exist as a compatibility pointer to _MEMORY.md.
The minimum viable PREPARATION fileset is _STATUS.md, _CONTEXT.md, _DEPENDENCIES.md, _REFERENCES.md, and a placeholder _SEMANTIC.md.
The TASK+four-documents document kit consists of Datasheet.md, Specification.md, Guidance.md, and Procedure.md.
The valid lifecycle state sequence is OPEN to INITIALIZED to SEMANTIC_READY to IN_PROGRESS to CHECKING to ISSUED.
OPEN means the folder exists but has no content yet, typically triggered by PREPARATION creating the folder.
INITIALIZED means draft documents have been generated, typically triggered when TASK+four-documents completes the document kit.
SEMANTIC_READY means the semantic lens has been generated, typically triggered by TASK+semantic-matrix-build writing _SEMANTIC.md.
IN_PROGRESS means active human and agent work has begun.
CHECKING means the deliverable is under review after a human moves it to review.
ISSUED means the deliverable has been released after human approval and issue.
PREPARATION is authorized to transition a deliverable into OPEN.
TASK+four-documents is authorized to transition a deliverable from OPEN to INITIALIZED.
TASK+semantic-matrix-build is authorized to transition a deliverable from INITIALIZED to SEMANTIC_READY.
A human or WORKING_ITEMS may transition a deliverable from INITIALIZED to IN_PROGRESS when the semantic step is skipped.
A human or WORKING_ITEMS may transition a deliverable from SEMANTIC_READY to IN_PROGRESS.
Only a human is authorized to transition a deliverable from IN_PROGRESS to CHECKING.
Only a human is authorized to transition a deliverable from CHECKING to ISSUED.
_STATUS.md is the authoritative lifecycle indicator for deliverable state.
No file other than _STATUS.md determines deliverable state.
Stage gates such as 30, 60, 90, or IFC are human-managed milestones and are not lifecycle states.
Stage gates are tracked separately in coordination records.
_CONTEXT.md header fields must match the decomposition document exactly.
The Decomposition Reference in _CONTEXT.md must point to the specific decomposition document used.
_CONTEXT.md is created by PREPARATION and must not be modified by agents other than through permitted human edits.
_DEPENDENCIES.md is a hybrid container with human-owned and agent-owned zones.
PREPARATION creates the human-owned dependency sections, and humans or ORCHESTRATOR maintain them.
Human-owned dependency sections include Dependency Tracking Mode, Declared Upstream, and Declared Downstream.
TASK+dependency-extract populates the agent-owned dependency sections.
Agent-owned dependency sections include Extracted Dependency Register, Run Notes and History, Lifecycle Summary, and Consumer Handoff Notes.
The Dependency Tracking Mode field accepts NOT_TRACKED, DECLARED, or TRACKED.
_DEPENDENCIES.md points to Dependencies.csv using schema v3.1.
NOT_TRACKED means dependencies are coordinated externally by humans.
DECLARED means only human-declared upstream and downstream dependencies are tracked, with no agent extraction.
TRACKED means full extraction is performed via TASK+dependency-extract and Dependencies.csv is present.
The RegisterSchemaVersion column must be present in every Dependencies.csv row and set to v3.1.
The DependencyID column is required and must be unique within the deliverable register.
The FromPackageID column is required and stores the package ID of the host deliverable.
The FromDeliverableID column is required and stores the deliverable ID of the host deliverable.
The FromDeliverableName column is required and stores the human-readable name of the host deliverable.
The DependencyClass column is required and must be ANCHOR or EXECUTION.
The AnchorType column is required and uses the canonical enum values defined in Section 6.3.
The Direction column is required and must be UPSTREAM or DOWNSTREAM.
The DependencyType column is required and uses the canonical enum values defined in Section 6.3.
The TargetType column is required and uses the canonical enum values defined in Section 6.3.
The TargetPackageID column is optional and stores the target package ID when the target is a deliverable.
The TargetDeliverableID column is optional and stores the stable deliverable ID when TargetType is DELIVERABLE.
The TargetRefID column is optional and stores a stable reference ID for non-deliverable targets.
The TargetName column should provide a human-readable target name or description.
The TargetLocation column optionally stores a path, URL, or document identifier for the target.
The Statement column should provide a human-readable dependency statement.
The EvidenceFile column must identify the source document containing evidence or use location TBD.
The SourceRef column must provide a path plus heading or section within the evidence file, or use location TBD.
The EvidenceQuote column should provide a traceability quote of no more than 30 words.
The Explicitness column should classify a dependency as EXPLICIT or IMPLICIT.
The RequiredMaturity column optionally records the maturity level required for dependency satisfaction.
The ProposedMaturity column optionally records an agent-suggested maturity level.
The SatisfactionStatus column should use the canonical satisfaction enum values defined in Section 6.3.
The Confidence column should classify evidence confidence as HIGH, MEDIUM, or LOW.
The Origin column is required and must be DECLARED or EXTRACTED.
The FirstSeen column is required and uses the ISO YYYY-MM-DD date of first extraction.
The LastSeen column is required and uses the ISO YYYY-MM-DD date of most recent confirmation.
The Status column is required and must be ACTIVE or RETIRED.
The Notes column is optional and may include explanatory remarks or epistemic labels such as FACT, ASSUMPTION, or PROPOSAL.
Extension columns may be present in Dependencies.csv without breaking compatibility.
EstimateImpactClass is an extension column with values BLOCKING, ADVISORY, INFO, and TBD.
ConsumerHint is an extension column with values TASK, TASK_ESTIMATING, AGGREGATION, RECONCILIATION, and TBD.
ANCHOR is a DependencyClass value for tree edges that connect deliverables to definition or traceability nodes.
EXECUTION is a DependencyClass value for DAG edges representing information flow, prerequisites, handoffs, or constraints.
IMPLEMENTS_NODE is an AnchorType value for a parent definition node, with exactly one per deliverable.
TRACES_TO_REQUIREMENT is an AnchorType value for zero or more requirement trace links.
NOT_APPLICABLE is an AnchorType value used for EXECUTION rows.
UPSTREAM means the deliverable requires information from the target.
DOWNSTREAM means the deliverable produces information for the target.
PREREQUISITE is the preferred DependencyType for required input or approval before work can proceed.
INTERFACE is the preferred DependencyType for explicit data or artifact exchange between deliverables.
HANDOVER is the preferred DependencyType for output of one deliverable consumed as input to another.
CONSTRAINT is the preferred DependencyType for an explicit constraint or condition.
ENABLES is the preferred DependencyType when a deliverable enables downstream work.
OTHER is the preferred DependencyType for dependencies that do not fit other categories and for ANCHOR rows.
COORDINATION is a legacy DependencyType that must not be emitted in new extractions.
INFORMATION is a legacy DependencyType that must not be emitted directly in new extractions.
DELIVERABLE is a TargetType for another deliverable in the project.
PACKAGE is a TargetType for a package and is used in ANCHOR rows.
WBS_NODE is a TargetType for a work breakdown structure or scope node.
REQUIREMENT is a TargetType for a specific requirement such as a SOW item or objective.
DOCUMENT is a TargetType for an external or reference document.
EQUIPMENT is a TargetType for physical equipment or assets.
EXTERNAL is a TargetType for an external entity, organization, standard, or similar target.
UNKNOWN is a TargetType for targets that cannot be confidently resolved.
EXPLICIT means the dependency is directly stated in source text.
IMPLICIT means the dependency is implied but not directly stated.
TBD means SatisfactionStatus has not yet been assessed.
PENDING means SatisfactionStatus has been assessed but not yet satisfied.
IN_PROGRESS means SatisfactionStatus is actively being worked toward satisfaction.
SATISFIED means the dependency has been fulfilled.
WAIVED means the dependency was waived by human decision.
NOT_APPLICABLE means the dependency was determined not to be applicable.
HIGH confidence means strong evidence with an explicit source reference.
MEDIUM confidence means reasonable evidence with some interpretation required.
LOW confidence means weak evidence with significant interpretation or assumption.
DECLARED origin means the dependency was human-declared.
EXTRACTED origin means the dependency was extracted by an agent from source documents.
ACTIVE status means the dependency is currently observed and relevant.
RETIRED status means the dependency was previously observed but is no longer found in source text.
ANCHOR rows connect a deliverable to the project's definition tree.
Exactly one IMPLEMENTS_NODE row should exist per deliverable.
Zero or more TRACES_TO_REQUIREMENT rows may connect a deliverable to scope items, objectives, or requirements.
DependencyType must be OTHER for ANCHOR rows.
AnchorType must not be NOT_APPLICABLE for ANCHOR rows.
EXECUTION rows capture information flow and constraints.
EXECUTION rows must have DependencyClass set to EXECUTION.
EXECUTION rows must have AnchorType set to NOT_APPLICABLE.
EXECUTION rows use the preferred execution DependencyType enums PREREQUISITE, INTERFACE, HANDOVER, CONSTRAINT, ENABLES, and OTHER.
Every ACTIVE dependency row must include EvidenceFile identifying the source document or location TBD.
Every ACTIVE dependency row must include SourceRef identifying the path plus heading or section, or location TBD.
EvidenceQuote should be provided for traceability with a maximum of 30 words.
Each dependency row tracks an extraction lifecycle and a closure lifecycle.
The extraction lifecycle includes FirstSeen, LastSeen, and Status.
FirstSeen records the date the dependency row was first created.
LastSeen records the date the dependency row was most recently confirmed by extraction.
Status records whether a dependency row is ACTIVE or RETIRED in the extraction lifecycle.
The closure lifecycle includes RequiredMaturity, ProposedMaturity, and SatisfactionStatus.
RequiredMaturity records the maturity level needed for dependency satisfaction.
ProposedMaturity records the agent-suggested maturity level for dependency satisfaction.
SatisfactionStatus records the current satisfaction state of a dependency.
Dependency rows are never deleted.
Rows no longer observed in source text are marked RETIRED.
Legacy Direction value INBOUND normalizes to canonical UPSTREAM.
Legacy Direction value OUTBOUND normalizes to canonical DOWNSTREAM.
Legacy DependencyType value COORDINATION normalizes to canonical OTHER.
Legacy DependencyType value INFORMATION must be interpreted and mapped to PREREQUISITE, INTERFACE, HANDOVER, CONSTRAINT, or ENABLES as appropriate.
If RegisterSchemaVersion is missing from an existing file, it is added on write and set to v3.1.
DependencyID must be unique within a single deliverable's register.
DependencyID uses the format DEP-{PKG}-{DEL}-{SEQ}.
FromDeliverableID must match the host deliverable's ID.
When TargetType is DELIVERABLE, TargetDeliverableID must contain the target's stable deliverable ID.
For non-deliverable targets, TargetDeliverableID must be empty and TargetRefID and TargetName are used instead.
References are listed as relative paths where preferred, or as absolute paths to source documents.
Each reference entry includes a brief relevance statement.
_REFERENCES.md is created by PREPARATION and may be updated by a human or ORCHESTRATOR.
TASK+dependency-extract reads _REFERENCES.md but must not modify it.
_MEMORY.md is created by PREPARATION as an empty structured template.
_MEMORY.md is used by WORKING_ITEMS and deliverable-local task agents to record working context.
_MEMORY.md sections may be added as needed, but the listed sections are the minimum schema.
MEMORY.md may exist as a compatibility pointer containing 'See _MEMORY.md (canonical deliverable memory).'.
All AGENT_*.md instruction files must follow the structure defined by AGENT_HELPS_HUMANS.md.
Agent instruction files require the [[DOC:AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS]] document tag in the header.
Agent instruction files require the title pattern AGENT INSTRUCTIONS - {AGENT_NAME} ({Brief Descriptor}).
Agent instruction files require an AGENT_TYPE body header with value 0, 1, or 2.
The Agent Type table records AGENT_TYPE, AGENT_CLASS, INTERACTION_SURFACE, WRITE_SCOPE, BLOCKING, and PRIMARY_OUTPUTS.
Every agent instruction file must include PROTOCOL markers for execution procedure.
Every agent instruction file must include SPEC markers for validity requirements.
Every agent instruction file must include STRUCTURE markers for schemas, templates, and artifact definitions.
Every agent instruction file must include RATIONALE markers for non-normative interpretation and values.
When agent instruction sections conflict, precedence is PROTOCOL over SPEC over STRUCTURE over RATIONALE.
AGENT_TYPE valid values are TYPE 0, TYPE 1, and TYPE 2.
AGENT_CLASS valid values are PERSONA and TASK.
INTERACTION_SURFACE valid values are chat, INIT-TASK, spawned, and both.
WRITE_SCOPE valid values include repo-wide, deliverable-local, tool-root-only, workspace-scaffold-only, repo-metadata-only, and none.
BLOCKING valid values are never and allowed.
Use AGENT_* when referring to instruction files.
Use the role name when referring to the agent itself.
Harness runtime metadata parsing uses a split contract between YAML frontmatter and the canonical body header/table.
Runtime YAML frontmatter may provide description, subagents, tools, model, max_turns, disallowed_tools, and auto_approve_tools.
The canonical body header/table provides the AGENT_TYPE line and AGENT_CLASS value.
Delegated subagents must declare AGENT_TYPE: 2 in the body header.
AGENT_CLASS: TASK is preferred for delegated subagents and validated as a warning-level rule.
Runtime injects subagents only when CHIRALITY_ENABLE_SUBAGENTS is true and a Type 1 persona is allowlisted for subagents.
Runtime injects subagents only if opts.subagentGovernance is present and valid.
Valid subagentGovernance requires contextSealed to be true.
Valid subagentGovernance requires pipelineRunApproved to be true.
Valid subagentGovernance requires approvalRef to be a non-empty string.
approvedBy is optional in subagentGovernance metadata.
Missing or invalid governance metadata must block subagent injection while allowing the parent turn to continue normally.
POST /api/harness/turn accepts opts and applies runtime option mapping.
POST /api/harness/session/boot accepts opts while bootstrap policy remains authoritative for bootstrap-only constraints.
POST /api/harness/turn accepts optional attachments as an array of absolute filesystem path strings.
The UI sends attachment paths only; server-side runtime classifies and reads files.
Client-supplied attachment metadata is non-authoritative and must not be trusted for execution.
A turn may omit text when attachments are present.
Resolver validation is server-side and enforces supported attachment extensions.
Supported attachment extensions are .png, .jpg, .jpeg, .gif, .webp, .pdf, .txt, .md, and .csv.
Resolver validation rejects directories, symlinks, and special files by requiring stats.isFile().
Resolver validation enforces a 10 MB per-file size limit.
Resolver validation enforces an 18 MB total per-turn raw-byte budget.
Partial attachment failure is non-fatal when at least one attachment resolves or user text exists.
If all attachments fail and user text is empty, the request is rejected with 400.
When there are no attachments, runtime uses SDK query with a string prompt.
When attachments are present, runtime builds multimodal content blocks and uses SDK query with an AsyncIterable prompt.
The UI stores Attachment records for preview purposes only and the server reclassifies attachments.
On send failure, the UI rolls back the optimistic user message and streaming placeholder while preserving the draft and attachment selections.
Session rehydration validates attachment shape, silently drops malformed records, and restores valid records.
The UI may expose any subset of supported opts fields.
Omitted opts fields must follow runtime fallback chains.
UI visibility of a field must not be interpreted as runtime authorization.
Model selection falls back from opts.model to the global model to the runtime default.
Tool selection falls back from opts.tools to persona tools frontmatter to the runtime preset.
Max turns falls back from opts.maxTurns to persona max_turns frontmatter to the runtime default.
The UI may present delegation governance fields for operator use.
Runtime gate and seal logic remains authoritative for delegation governance.
Supplying opts.subagentGovernance does not guarantee delegation because all runtime gates must still pass.
Sanitize(name) replaces slash, backslash, colon, asterisk, question mark, quote, angle brackets, and pipe with hyphens.
Sanitize(name) collapses consecutive whitespace to a single space.
Sanitize(name) trims leading and trailing whitespace.
Package folders use {PKG-ID}_{Sanitize(PackageName)}/.
Deliverable folders use {DEL-ID}_{Sanitize(DeliverableName)}/.
Canonical unsanitized names are recorded in _CONTEXT.md.
Task agents that produce outputs to tool roots should write to timestamped snapshot folders.
Snapshot folder paths follow {TOOL_ROOT}/{SNAPSHOT_LABEL}_{YYYY-MM-DD}_{HHmm}/.
Snapshot folders are immutable after creation.
Reruns create new snapshot folders.
_LATEST.md is a mutable pointer file referencing the most recent snapshot.
_LATEST.md includes Latest and Updated fields.
Pointer files may be overwritten, but snapshots must not be overwritten.
An execution root is valid when at least one PKG-XX_{Label}/ folder exists.
An execution root is valid when _Decomposition/ exists and contains at least one decomposition document.
An execution root is valid when INIT.md exists with session parameters.
A package folder is valid when named {PKG-ID}_{PkgLabel}/ with a valid PKG-XX identifier.
A package folder is valid when it contains a 1_Working/ subfolder.
0_References/, 2_Checking/, and 3_Issued/ subfolders should exist in a package folder.
A deliverable folder is valid when named {DEL-ID}_{DelLabel}/ with a valid DEL-XX-YY identifier.
A deliverable folder is valid when it contains _STATUS.md with a valid lifecycle state.
A deliverable folder is valid when it contains _CONTEXT.md with header fields matching the decomposition.
A deliverable folder is valid when it contains _DEPENDENCIES.md.
A deliverable folder is valid when it contains _REFERENCES.md.
A deliverable folder is initialized when it additionally contains Datasheet.md, Specification.md, Guidance.md, and Procedure.md.
A deliverable folder is dependency-tracked when it additionally contains Dependencies.csv with valid v3.1 schema headers.
_COORDINATION.md is located at {EXECUTION_ROOT}/_Coordination/_COORDINATION.md.
_COORDINATION.md records the project's chosen coordination representation.
Schedule-first coordination means a Gantt drives sequencing while dependency tracking remains active for blocker detection and audit.
Dependency-tracked coordination means the dependency graph drives sequencing.
Hybrid coordination combines schedule-first and dependency-tracked coordination.
The coordination representation is chosen per project instance and recorded once.
The coordination representation does not change dependency tracking mechanics, which always maintain the full DAG.
The UI Navigation and Selector Contract defines deterministic frontend behavior for matrix launch routing and work mode selectors.
Desktop UI labels may be abbreviated variants of canonical agent or role names.
The selector list currently includes DEPENDENCIES as an archived wrapper name pointing to skills/dependency-extract/.
Full normalization of UI labels and removal of archived wrapper references is deferred to a separate frontend slice.
PORTAL matrix row NORMATIVE routes to WORKBENCH.
PORTAL matrix row OPERATIVE routes to PIPELINE.
PORTAL matrix row EVALUATIVE routes to WORKBENCH.
Matrix columns are shared labels GUIDING, APPLYING, JUDGING, and REVIEWING.
The WORKBENCH persona selector is limited to NORMATIVE and EVALUATIVE matrix agents.
The WORKBENCH persona selector includes HELP, ORCHESTRATE, WORKING_ITEMS, AGGREGATE, AGENTS, DEPENDENCIES, CHANGE, and RECONCILING.
OPERATIVE matrix entries must route to PIPELINE rather than WORKBENCH.
PIPELINE uses category-driven selectors.
PIPELINE Category values are DECOMP*, PREP*, TASK*, and AUDIT*.
PIPELINE Type uses category-specific static options, including disabled placeholders.
TASK-only PIPELINE split controls include Task Agent, Scope Mode, Scope, and Target Deliverable.
PIPELINE Scope Mode values are DELIVERABLES and KNOWLEDGE_TYPES.
Target Deliverable is required when PIPELINE Scope Mode is KNOWLEDGE_TYPES.
Requested but unsupported UI variants must be shown and disabled.
Disabled UI variants must remain visible to operators.
Disabled UI variants must be non-selectable.
Disabled UI variants must be labeled as coming soon or with an equivalent disabled hint.
Frontend state must clear invalid or stale selections when the project root changes.
Frontend state must clear invalid or stale selections when deliverable scan results no longer include the selected deliverable key.
Frontend state must clear knowledge-type scope selection when the knowledge decomposition marker is absent.
Frontend state must clear invalid or stale selections when a knowledge type no longer resolves to available target deliverables.
The /api/project/deliverables endpoint continues to return deliverables[] and is extended with knowledge-scope metadata.
Each deliverables[] item includes id, name, pkg, status, and path fields.
The knowledgeDecomposition response object includes enabled and markerFile fields.
The knowledgeTypes response array contains entries with id, label, and matchingDeliverableKeys fields.
knowledgeDecomposition.enabled is true only when a knowledge decomposition marker is found in decomposition docs.
knowledgeDecomposition.markerFile is the path or filename of the first marker-bearing decomposition file, or null when none is found.
Each knowledgeTypes[] element represents a canonical knowledge-type bucket observed across scanned deliverables.
knowledgeTypes[].id is the stable key for the knowledge type.
knowledgeTypes[].label is the human-readable label for the knowledge type.
knowledgeTypes[].matchingDeliverableKeys contains deliverable composite keys in pkg::id format where the type is present.
Knowledge types should be derived from canonical deliverable file classes.
Canonical knowledge types include Datasheet, Specification, Guidance, Procedure, Dependencies, References, Context, Status, Semantic, and Memory.
When knowledgeDecomposition.enabled is false, clients must not present knowledge-type scope as an active selection mode.
